scoring_justification: Pure CO2 isotherms and mixture data are only available as figures in the paper; exact numerical gold cannot be reconstructed without digitising. Structural trends (monotonicity, saturation bounds, peak location) are robust and prevent fabricating values without running the simulation. A numeric check on the zero‑loading Qst uses the paper’s stated value.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper‑reported saturation loading range and zero‑loading isosteric heat value for CO2 on silicalite.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: saturation 3.4–3.7 mmol/g; zero‑loading Qst ≈ 23.5 kJ/mol.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the conclusion and discussion sections of the paper.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These numbers are directly quoted from the paper and are used as reference bounds/targets.

outputs.description: Pure CO₂ absolute and excess adsorption isotherms. One row per simulated (T,P) point (3 temperatures × ~10 pressures).
Isosteric heat of adsorption as a function of CO₂ absolute loading. At least 10 rows spanning the loading range.
Benzene/CO₂ mixture adsorption isotherms at bulk benzene mole fraction 0.001. One row per simulated (T,P) point (2 temperatures × ≥5 pressures).
CO₂ self‑diffusion coefficients in the benzene/CO₂ mixture at 328.2 K. One row for each of the five simulated pressures (e.g. 3, 5, 9, 12, 15 MPa).

output_contract.notes: All scored files are compared to hidden gold values or structural checks. The binary interaction parameter fitting and P-R EOS calculations are included as process steps; their correctness is enforced through the load‑bearing mixture isotherm check.
